lead.name: ssn-1l-tag
lead.source: pouw_space.toml at N-CARD's f697396586 (cursor/compute-research-np-card-7c2d): S - 1 + c coin bits a row in whole 32-bit coin words (ssn-1l-hw's S + 15 fill the same words at Llama's K), B' lane 31 a public weight lane; T1 0.000% credited, 0.420% with the coins' XOF hashing uncredited (NIGHT.md section 7). ssn-1l-tag as built (N-KERNEL's 1034Z report, checked exact on the H200): step 1's lanes 0-23 hold A's data, 24-27 the row tag T(i), the balanced base-13 digits of z_i = (floor(i/2) + 1)(-1)^i, against G[0..3, j], and 28-31 the row's code bits a_1[i] against C; G is drawn per call after B, column j's from coin word m H + j of the call's stream, v = floor(u 2401 / 2^32), G[e, j] = v's base-7 digit e minus 3; S = 1 + ceil((K - 24)/31), 67 and 265 at Llama's K

layouts.source: blc1a: the coin on its own lane (lane 30) against a constant A' = 1, beside the lead's row-bit lane 31, at 30 data lanes a later step: its served noise sum_t s_t[tile, j] is a column term, folded by N-EXACT's IADD3 column source with the per-tile column vector streamed by the certifier (4 bytes a tile and column), or the coin itself where a tile carries coins in one step; the constant lane is static in A's layout (no forming, estimate). blc4a: three such coin lanes (28-30) beside the row lane 31, at 28 data lanes, one 4-byte cp.async a (tile, step, column) carrying the three coins and lane 31's public weight, no register written, served exactly by the same fold. B-lane coins: the B' noise lane of every later k32 step holds a nonzero coin value per (row tile, step, column), odd in +-(2^e - 1), streamed raw by the certifier; one lane (blc1, the lead's own lane) is patched into the B tile in shared memory by one 32-bit load a 4 coin bytes and four byte stores; four lanes (blc4, lanes 28-31) take a 4-byte cp.async a column a later step, no register written, at 28 data lanes a later step. A wgmma's B tile is shared by the CTA tile's rows (64 a warpgroup, 128 for two), so a coin entry is shared by them. blc1a and blc4a put lane coins on step 1 too (its 4 tag lanes, 4 code lanes, the L coin lanes and 24 - L data lanes), since a step-1 word reads only the row's code bits and its tag's G digits otherwise, which a large call's rows share; a tile with r < T rows carries ceil(S r / T) steps' worth of them, on step 1 and spread evenly over its steps, one lane or two a step for blc4a, so that no run of steps without lane coins is longer than it must be: the words of a step interval read only the accumulators' coin state before it (for blc1a / blc4a a row term and a column term, at least one e-bit coin a tile and column) and the interval's own coins. blc1 and blc4, for reference, carry theirs in ceil((S - 1) r / T) later steps, spread evenly, and none on step 1. In the rest blc1 keeps the lead's public lane, whose increment (1 + b_t) 1 has p* = 1/2 under A2c / A8; blc1a and blc4a put a uniform fill_row_coin_bits-bit row coin r_t(i) in the row lane against the public 1 instead of 1 + b_t(i), streamed raw beside the row bits, and a window coin c_t[j] (odd in +-(2^fill_window_coin_bits - 1), drawn after B is committed) in B' lane 30 against A' = 1, written into B's padded lane once a window: a row term and a column term the same fold removes (sum_t c_t[j] over a call's coin-less steps is the window's total less its coin steps', n adds a coin step). A step's increment r_t(i) + c_t[j] has p* = 2^-8 even where the call's data, chosen after the window coin, cancels c on its data lanes' worth of columns; and since c differs across columns, a one-row tile's run of such steps can't repeat whole row vectors (N-ADAPT's walk) except on those columns, at copy_grain_words-word chunks (CopyGrain(4)). C-init: an accumulator-init coin an output element, e = ceil(K / n_target) bits

prices.source: W1 at H32 (a register write 32 units, a MAC 1); the hashing credit at ShaLB's 3,632 registers a 128-byte compression (the alt_roads floor, 908 units a byte) and N-SHALB's 3,532 for chained compressions (NIGHT.md section 7); answers: DitherInstance's W_mac bounds W_mm + W_sha + W_ans, the selected blocks' answers at full weight, which N-CARD prices at none (0 here, a lower estimate); byte stores into shared memory are unpriced in W1 and timed at one a lane a SM-clock (estimate)

outsource.source: The outsourcing provers under R1b: the prover keeps A_j for the certifier, so it computes the served path itself and an outside machine computes the coin-dependent words and their hashing, returning one 512-bit root a call. With a coin-free served path (the de-noised lead, blc1a) the outside machine rebuilds the activations from the 32-bit token and takes any set of call types; with a noisy one it needs the coins of every earlier call (a prefix of the forward). The cap's slack is the cap less the honest's own traffic, one 17-bit Llama-3 token id a token (128,256 ids, in for prefill or out for decode; estimate)

nred.source: N-RED interim 2 (note compute-research/20261029T0940Z-report-np-red): A2c on ssn-1l-tag (the later steps' (1 + b_t) 1 cancelled by one chosen data lane) saves 51.6% of stock at m 8,192 under W1 as N-W1 states it (model P), p* = max_v Pr[a step's coin increment = v] = 1/2. The calculator counts A8 / A2c itself (nred_round3's model P in expectation, per step type) and holds the lead's count to this point

certifier.source: SHA-512 counter-mode coins on one AMD EPYC Genoa core (runs r20261029-074951-e66c and r20261029-075358-9963)
